subject.title: [Bug]: Agents should not be able to access or modify files outside their own working space.

question: Should OpenClaw change the default agent filesystem/tool boundary so non-personal agents cannot read or write outside their workspace, or keep host-wide access as an explicit trusted-operator default?
rationale: Current code and docs make confinement opt-in; changing that default is a security boundary and compatibility decision, and a file-tool-only change does not settle exec/process access.

options.title: Define a secure default with migration
options.body: Use the existing `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` and sandbox surfaces where possible, but require an upgrade/docs plan and coverage for exec/process boundaries before closing this issue.

options.title: Keep trusted-host default
options.body: Leave host-wide access as the default and improve audit/docs warnings, accepting that this issue remains a documented trust-model tradeoff rather than a bug fix.

options.title: Land partial filesystem hardening first
options.body: Review focused PRs like the relative traversal and PathGuard work as incremental hardening while keeping this issue open for the broader boundary decision.

recommendation.title: Define a secure default with migration
recommendation.body: Use the existing `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` and sandbox surfaces where possible, but require an upgrade/docs plan and coverage for exec/process boundaries before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the current opt-in filesystem policy and recent area code is Peter Steinberger's commits.
